column1: Discovered in the early 1800s and named nicotianine, the oily essence now called nicotine is the main active ingredient of tobacco.
column2: 19世纪初发现并命名为烟草香素的油状物质，如今被称为尼古丁，是烟草的主要活性成分。

column1: Nicotine, however, is only a small component of cigarette smoke, which contains more than 4,700 chemical compounds, including 43 cancer-causing substances.
column2: 然而，尼古丁只是香烟烟雾中的一小部分成分，烟雾中含有超过4700种化学物质，其中包含43种致癌物。

column1: In recent times, scientific research has been providing evidence that years of cigarette smoking vastly increases the risk of developing fatal medical conditions.
column2: 近年来，科学研究表明，长期吸烟会显著增加罹患致命疾病的风险。

column1: In addition to being responsible for more than 85 per cent of lung cancers, smoking is associated with cancers of, amongst others, the mouth, stomach and kidneys, and is thought to cause about 14 per cent of leukemia and cervical cancers.
column2: 除了导致超过85%的肺癌外，吸烟还与口腔、胃和肾脏等癌症有关，并被认为导致约14%的白血病和宫颈癌。
column3: In addition to|prep. 除了...之外

column1: In 1990, smoking caused more than 84,000 deaths, mainly resulting from such problems as pneumonia, bronchitis and influenza.
column2: 在1990年，吸烟导致了超过84,000人死亡，这些死亡主要由肺炎、支气管炎和流感等问题引起。

column1: Smoking, it is believed, is responsible for 30 per cent of all deaths from cancer and clearly represents the most important preventable cause of cancer in countries like the United States today.
column2: 据认为，吸烟是导致所有癌症死亡病例中30%的原因，在像美国这样的国家里，吸烟显然是最重要且可预防的癌症诱因。

column1: Passive smoking, the breathing in of the side-stream smoke from the burning of tobacco between puffs or of the smoke exhaled by a smoker, also causes a serious health risk.
column2: 被动吸烟，即吸入烟草燃烧产生的侧流烟或吸烟者呼出的烟雾，也会带来严重的健康风险。

column1: A report published in 1992 by the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) emphasized the health dangers, especially from side-stream smoke.
column2: 美国环境保护署1992年发布的一份报告强调了健康风险，尤其是来自侧流烟的健康危害。

column1: This type of smoke contains more, smaller particles and is therefore more likely to be deposited deep in the lungs.
column2: 这种烟雾中含有更多、更细小的颗粒物，因此更容易沉积在肺部深处。

column1: On the basis of this report, the EPA has classified environmental tobacco smoke in the highest risk category for causing cancer.
column2: 根据这份报告，美国环保署将环境烟草烟归类为致癌风险最高的类别。

column1: As an illustration of the health risks, in the case of a married couple where one partner is a smoker and one a non-smoker, the latter is believed to have a 30 per cent higher risk of death from heart disease because of passive smoking.
column2: 以健康风险为例，一对夫妻中，若一人吸烟、一人不吸烟，据认为，不吸烟的一方会因被动吸烟而使死于心脏病的风险升高30%。
column10: higher risk of death|n. 更高的死亡风险

column1: The risk of lung cancer also increases over the years of exposure and the figure jumps to 80 per cent if the spouse has been smoking four packs a day for 20 years.
column2: 接触二手烟的年数越长，患肺癌的风险也越高。如果配偶连续20年每天吸四包烟，这一数字便跃升至80%。
column3: risk of lung cancer|n. 患肺癌的风险
column9: four packs a day|每天四包

column1: It has been calculated that 17 per cent of cases of lung cancer can be attributed to high levels of exposure to second-hand tobacco smoke during childhood and adolescence.
column2: 计算显示，儿童和青少年时期暴露于高水平二手烟草烟雾，可导致17%的肺癌病例。

column1: A more recent study by researchers at the University of California at San Francisco (UCSF) has shown that second-hand cigarette smoke does more harm to non-smokers than to smokers.
column2: 加州大学旧金山分校的研究人员最近的一项研究表明，二手烟对非吸烟者的危害比对吸烟者要大得多。

column1: Leaving aside the philosophical question of whether anyone should have to breathe someone else’s cigarette smoke, the report suggests that the smoke experienced by many people in their daily lives is enough to produce substantial adverse effects on a person’s heart and lungs.
column2: 暂且不说是否应该让某人吸入他人的香烟烟雾这一哲学问题，该报告指出，许多人在日常生活中所接触的烟雾足以对人们的心脏和肺部造成严重的损害。

column1: The report, published in the Journal of the American Medical Association (AMA), was based on the researchers’ own earlier research but also includes a review of studies over the past few years.
column2: 这份报告发表于《美国医学会杂志》，以研究人员自己此前的研究为基础，也综述了过去几年的其他研究。
column5: American Medical Association|n. 美国医学会
column9: over the past few years|在过去几年里

column1: The American Medical Association represents about half of all US doctors and is a strong opponent of smoking.
column2: 美国医学协会代表着大约一半的美国医生，该组织是吸烟问题的强烈反对者。

column1: The study suggests that people who smoke cigarettes are continually damaging their cardiovascular system, which adapts in order to compensate for the effects of smoking.
column2: 研究表明，吸烟的人会持续损害自己的心血管系统，而人体会通过自我调整来弥补吸烟带来的负面影响。

column1: It further states that people who do not smoke do not have the benefit of their system adapting to the smoke inhalation.
column2: 它进一步指出，不吸烟的人无法享受到身体系统因长期接触烟雾而带来的适应性好处。

column1: Consequently, the effects of passive smoking are far greater on non-smokers than on smokers.
column2: 因此，就被动吸烟造成的影响而言，不吸烟者受到的影响远大于吸烟者。

column1: This report emphasizes that cancer is not caused by a single element in cigarette smoke; harmful effects to health are caused by many components.
column2: 这份报告强调，香烟烟雾中致癌的成分并非只有一种，多种成分都会危害健康。

column1: Carbon monoxide, for example, competes with oxygen in red blood cells and interferes with the blood’s ability to deliver life giving oxygen to the heart.
column2: 例如，一氧化碳会与红细胞中的氧气竞争，从而干扰血液向心脏输送氧气的能力。

column1: Nicotine and other toxins in cigarette smoke activate small blood cells called platelets, which increases the likelihood of blood clots, thereby affecting blood circulation throughout the body.
column2: 香烟中的尼古丁及其他有害物质会激活血液中的血小板，从而增加血液凝结的可能性，进而影响全身的血液循环。

column1: The researchers criticize the practice of some scientific consultants who work with the tobacco industry for assuming that cigarette smoke has the same impact on smokers as it does on non-smokers.
column2: 研究人员批评了一些与烟草行业合作的科学顾问的做法，他们错误地认为香烟烟雾对吸烟者和非吸烟者的影响相同。

column1: They argue that those scientists are underestimating the damage done by passive smoking and, in support of their recent findings, cite some previous research which points to passive smoking as the cause for between 30,000 and 60,000 deaths from heart attacks each year in the United States.
column2: 他们认为，那些科学家低估了被动吸烟造成的危害。为支持最近的研究结果，他们引用了此前的一些研究，其中的证据指向被动吸烟：美国每年有3万至6万人因心脏病发作而死亡，可归因于被动吸烟。

column1: This means that passive smoking is the third most preventable cause of death after active smoking and alcohol-related diseases.
column2: 这意味着，被动吸烟是第三大可预防的死亡原因，仅次于主动吸烟和与酒精相关的疾病。

column1: The study argues that the type of action needed against passive smoking should be similar to that being taken against illegal drugs and AIDS (SIDA).
column2: 该研究认为，针对被动吸烟所采取的行动方式，应该与针对非法毒品和艾滋病所采取的措施类似。

column1: The UCSF researchers maintain that the simplest and most cost-effective action is to establish smoke-free work places, schools and public places.
column2: 加州大学旧金山分校的研究人员认为，最简单且最经济的举措是建立无烟的工作场所、学校和公共场所。
